y-m-50-04.title: If composite function na one-to-one, both functions too na one-to-one?
y-m-50-04.topic: Wetin we fit talk about f and g when composite function g∘f na one-to-one
y-m-50-04.goal: Find composite-function values directly from the given table to test Eunsu claim, and explain how counterexample break one part of the claim while the other part still hold.
y-m-50-04.material:
Sets X={1, 2}, Y={a, b, c}, Z={p, q, r} dey. Functions f: X→Y and g: Y→Z be these.
f(1)=a, f(2)=b
g(a)=p, g(b)=q, g(c)=p
Composite function g∘f connect element x of X to g(f(x)). One-to-one function mean different elements of domain always connect to different values.
Eunsu claim: "If g∘f na one-to-one function, then both f and g na one-to-one functions."
y-m-50-04.thinking.0: Split the claim into two parts and judge each one separately
y-m-50-04.thinking.2: Explain the reason for the part wey hold
y-m-50-04.prereq.0: 'H1' for this task na only difficulty label for the production assignment; e no mean say curriculum dey teach this content for any particular class. Premise: assume say you know wetin function mean, how to find composite-function value (g∘f)(x)=g(f(x)), and wetin one-to-one function mean (different domain elements always connect to different values). One-to-one correspondence and inverse functions no dey used.
y-m-50-04.s.s1.prompt: Find the values of g∘f directly for f and g above, then choose wetin this example show about Eunsu claim.
y-m-50-04.s.s1.hint.0: Find g∘f(1) and g∘f(2) separately and arrange dem for table.
y-m-50-04.s.s1.hint.1: Check whether any of the three values g(a), g(b), g(c) for g equal one another.
y-m-50-04.s.s1.o.a: If g∘f na one-to-one, g too gats be one-to-one
y-m-50-04.s.s1.r.a: Compare g(a) and g(c). Check whether this g get two different elements wey give the same value.
y-m-50-04.s.s1.o.b: For this example, g∘f no be one-to-one function
y-m-50-04.s.s1.r.b: Calculate g(f(1)) and g(f(2)) directly and check if dem equal. Check whether you make your judgment before calculating.
y-m-50-04.s.s1.o.c: Even if g∘f na one-to-one, g fit no be one-to-one
y-m-50-04.s.s1.o.d: c no dey among the values of f, so you no need to consider g(c) for this example
y-m-50-04.s.s1.r.d: To check whether g na one-to-one, you gats examine every element for domain Y of g. Also check the value g get for c, wey no dey among the values of f.
y-m-50-04.s.s1.explain: g∘f(1)=g(a)=p and g∘f(2)=g(b)=q, so g∘f na one-to-one. But g(a)=g(c)=p, so g no be one-to-one. So this one example don break the part of the claim wey say 'g too'. One counterexample fit break 'always'.
y-m-50-04.s.s2.prompt: This time, make counterexample directly with numbers. X={1, 2}, Y={1, 2, 3}, Z={1, 2, 3}, and f(1)=1, f(2)=2. Choose values g(1)=u, g(2)=v, g(3)=w (each one na 1, 2, or 3), then make three different (u, v, w) wey go make g∘f one-to-one but g no be one-to-one.
y-m-50-04.s.s2.hint.0: First write as expression the kind of values g(f(1)) and g(f(2)) gats get for g∘f to be one-to-one.
y-m-50-04.s.s2.hint.1: For g no to be one-to-one, check wetin gats happen among values u, v, w; separately check whether g(3) dey among values of g∘f.
y-m-50-04.s.s2.ok.c1: All three values na elements of Z.
y-m-50-04.s.s2.fail.c1: Values of g gats be elements of Z={1, 2, 3} (one of 1, 2, 3).
y-m-50-04.s.s2.fail.c2: Compare g∘f(1)=g(f(1))=u and g∘f(2)=g(f(2))=v. For this case, g∘f no be one-to-one.
y-m-50-04.s.s2.fail.c3: u, v, w all different. Then g na one-to-one function wey give different values to three different inputs.
y-m-50-04.s.s2.explain: Values of g∘f na only u and v, so if u≠v, g∘f na one-to-one. For g not to be one-to-one, g(3)=w must equal u or v. Even if g repeat earlier value for 3, wey no show among f values, e no affect g∘f. If w different from u and v, g too become one-to-one, so e no fit be counterexample.
y-m-50-04.s.s3.prompt: The part of Eunsu claim wey say 'if g∘f na one-to-one, then f na one-to-one' correct. Explain why e correct.
y-m-50-04.s.s3.hint.0: Imagine one case where f no be one-to-one (f(1)=f(2)), then write the two g∘f values.
y-m-50-04.s.s3.hint.1: Use function definition check wetin g give when you put same value inside am.

y-m-50-04.s.s3.model.0: If f no be one-to-one, two different inputs fit get same value, like f(1)=f(2); putting dem inside g too give g(f(1))=g(f(2)), same value. Then g∘f no be one-to-one. So if g∘f na one-to-one, f must be one-to-one.
y-m-50-04.s.s3.model.1: g∘f values come from putting f values inside g. If f give same value two times, g give same answer for that value; so different inputs for g∘f too get same output. Then e no be one-to-one.
y-m-50-04.s.s3.modelNote.1: E explain with words without symbols, but e get same-value assumption and conclusion both.
y-m-50-04.s.s3.model.2: Same input only give same value, so g no fit split again two values wey f don join. So g∘f no fit be one-to-one too.

y-m-50-03.title: Move first then flip, or flip first then move: result go be the same?
y-m-50-03.topic: The order for translating a graph and reflecting am on x-axis (when both orders give the same result)
y-m-50-03.goal: Use one counterexample confirm say the graph wey result fit change based on whether you translate first or reflect on x-axis first; find by yourself when changing the order go give the same graph, and explain why using vertex position.
y-m-50-03.material:
Make two changes to graph of y=x², using different orders.
Method A: First reflect am on x-axis, then translate am p for x direction and q for y direction.
Method B: First translate am p for x direction and q for y direction, then reflect am on x-axis.
(Positive p mean move to the right and negative p to the left; positive q mean move up and negative q down. Reflection on x-axis mean flip am upside down.)
Minho talk say, "Even if you change the order, the graph wey result go always be the same."

y-m-50-03.s.s1.explain: A get vertex for (p, q) and e open downward; B get vertex for (p, -q) and e open downward. If q no be 0, the vertices y-coordinates different, so the graphs different. If q na 0, dem be the same graph for any p.

y-m-50-03.s.s3.model.0: For B, first we move the vertex to (p, q), then flip am, so the sign of the vertex y-coordinate change and e become (p, -q). For A, we move after the flip, so the vertex na (p, q). For q and -q to equal, q gats be 0; movement p for x direction no concern x-axis reflection, so p fit be any value.
y-m-50-03.s.s3.model.1: Reflection on x-axis dey flip things upside down. If you raise am by q, then flip am, e go move down by q; but if you flip am first, then raise am, e go stay up. So if q no be 0, vertex height go different, while moving sideways no effect.

y-m-50-06.topic: Number of times graph y=√(x-1)+2 meet line y=x+k (how e change as k change)
y-m-50-06.goal: Use actual values test the idea say number of crossings dey increase steadily as line move one direction; find some values wey meet condition and explain number depend on k range.
y-m-50-06.material:
Function graph f(x)=√(x-1)+2 (x≥1) start at point (1, 2) then slowly rise to right. (√ we read 'square root', and √(x-1) mean 'square root of x minus 1'.) Examples: f(1)=2, f(2)=3, f(5)=4, f(10)=5.
We move line y=x+k (slope 1, k constant) up and down. Seohyun say, 'If k increase, line go up, so number of points where e meet graph go keep increasing.'

y-m-50-06.prereq.0: 'H1' for this task na only difficulty label for production; no mean say curriculum teach content for particular grade. y-m-50-06.s.s1.r.d: Compare k=0 and k=1. Check how intersection number different for the two values.
y-m-50-06.s.s1.explain: If k=0, line y=x get f(2)=3>2 and f(5)=4<5, so e meet graph one time between x=2 and 5. If k=1, f(1)=2=1+1 and f(2)=3=2+1, so dem meet at x=1 and x=2 (two points). If k=2, line always above graph and dem no meet (0 point). So claim 'keeps increasing' get counterexample.

y-m-50-06.s.s2.explain: Set √(x-1)=t (t≥0), then t+2=t²+1+k, so t²-t+k-1=0. For two different intersections, we need two different nonnegative roots. Discriminant na 5-4k>0 and product of roots na k-1≥0; so 1≤k<5/4. If k=5/4 dem touch one point; if k<1 one point; if k>5/4 dem no meet.

y-m-50-02.material:
Jimin describe the graph of quadratic function y=ax²+bx+c (a, b, c na real numbers, a≠0) with words. No picture dey. Dem read the expression as 'y equals a times x squared plus b times x plus c'.
(가) The graph opens upward (is convex downward).
(나) The y-coordinate of the point where it meets the y-axis is 3.
(다) The vertex is to the right of the y-axis. (The x-coordinate of the vertex is positive.)
(라) It meets the x-axis at two different points.
